title: Rigveda 8.89: To Indra
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 8.89: To Indra: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 8.89 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to Indra. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 8, the book of the Kaṇva and Aṅgiras poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 652r-652v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 8.89.1-3 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 6, varga 12); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 652r
translation.original_text:
1bṛ̱had indrā̍ya gāyata̱ maru̍to vṛtra̱haṁta̍mam | yena̱ jyoti̱r aja̍nayann ṛtā̱vṛdho̍ de̱vaṁ de̱vāya̱ jāgṛ̍vi ||
2apā̍dhamad a̱bhiśa̍stīr aśasti̱hāthendro̍ dyu̱mny ābha̍vat | de̱vās ta̍ indra sa̱khyāya̍ yemire̱ bṛha̍dbhāno̱ maru̍dgaṇa ||
3pra va̱ indrā̍ya bṛha̱te maru̍to̱ brahmā̍rcata | vṛ̱traṁ ha̍nati vṛtra̱hā śa̱takra̍tu̱r vajre̍ṇa śa̱tapa̍rvaṇā ||
translation.text:
1To Indra sing the lofty hymn, Maruts that slays the Vr̥itras best. Whereby the Holy Ones created for the God the light divine that ever wakes.
2Indra who quells the curse blew curses far away, and then in splendour came to us. Indra, refulgent with thy Marut host! the Gods strove eagerly to win thy love.
3Sing to your lofty Indra, sing, Maruts, a holy hymn of praise. Let Ṣatakratu, Vr̥itra-slayer, kill the foe with hundred-knotted thunderbolt.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 652r (numbered 74r by the scribe) (OPenn image 652, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 8.88.4 ‹abhi majmanā ā tvā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 652v (numbered 74v by the scribe), begins in RV 8.89.4 ‹āpaḥ javasā vi mātaraḥ›. Verses 8.89.1-3 end on this page.

1bṛhat | indrāya | gāyata | marutaḥ | vṛtraham-tamam | yena | jyotiḥ | ajanayan | ṛta-vṛdhaḥ | devam | devāya | jāgṛvi
2apa | adhamat | abhi-śastīḥ | aśasti-hā | atha | indraḥ | dyumnī | ā | abhavat | devāḥ | te | indra | sakhyāyayemire | bṛhadbhāno itibṛhat-bhāno | marut-gaṇa
3pra | vaḥ | indrāya | bṛhate | marutaḥ | brahma | arcata | vṛtram | hanati | vṛtra-hā | śata-kratuḥ | vajreṇa | śata-parvaṇā

translation.original_ref: RV 8.89.4-7 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 6, varga 12); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 652v
translation.original_text:
4a̱bhi pra bha̍ra dhṛṣa̱tā dhṛ̍ṣanmana̱ḥ śrava̍ś cit te asad bṛ̱hat | arṣa̱ntv āpo̱ java̍sā̱ vi mā̱taro̱ hano̍ vṛ̱traṁ jayā̱ sva̍ḥ ||
5yaj jāya̍thā apūrvya̱ magha̍van vṛtra̱hatyā̍ya | tat pṛ̍thi̱vīm a̍prathaya̱s tad a̍stabhnā u̱ta dyām ||
6tat te̍ ya̱jño a̍jāyata̱ tad a̱rka u̱ta haskṛ̍tiḥ | tad viśva̍m abhi̱bhūr a̍si̱ yaj jā̱taṁ yac ca̱ jantva̍m ||
7ā̱māsu̍ pa̱kvam aira̍ya̱ ā sūrya̍ṁ rohayo di̱vi | gha̱rmaṁ na sāma̍n tapatā suvṛ̱ktibhi̱r juṣṭa̱ṁ girva̍ṇase bṛ̱hat ||
translation.text:
4Aim and fetch boldly forth, O thou whose heart is bold: great glory will be thine thereby. In rapid torrent let the mother waters spread. Slay Vr̥itra, win the light of heaven.
5When thou, unequalled Maghavan, wast born to smite the Vr̥itras dead, Thou spreadest out the spacious earth and didst support and prop the heavens.
6There was the sacrifice produced for thee, the laud, and song of joy, Thou in thy might surpassest all, all that now is and yet shall be.
7Raw kine thou filledst with ripe milk. Thou madest Sûrya rise to heaven. Heat him as milk is heated with pure Sâma hymns, great joy to him who loves the song.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 652v (numbered 74v by the scribe) (OPenn image 653, upper leaf). Verses 8.89.4-7 end on this page; 8.89.4 begins on fol. 652r (numbered 74r by the scribe).
